From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@catalyst.bio>

Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@catalyst.bio>, procurement@catalyst.bio
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps after demo — reliability/limits questions

Ben — thanks for the demo today, good overview. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering lead: 

- Can you share a short table of observed 99th-percentile latency at 1, 5, and 10 RPS for the 7B model you demoed?
- What happens when we hit the per-second rate limit? Do requests queue, reject, or get routed to a fallback?
- If a region has an outage, what failover behavior should we expect for a dedicated customer vs hosted?

We also need a rough timeline for running an interoperability test between Redwood and our hyperscaler endpoint (GCP Vertex) — specifically: throughput parity and failure behavior under burst. Procurement is copied for a potential PO timeline.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of ML Infrastructure
Catalyst Biotech

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@catalyst.bio>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina.patel@catalyst.bio>, procurement@catalyst.bio
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — reliability/limits questions

Jordan — great to hear, and appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front and then proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- 99p latency (7B / sequence ~256 tokens): ~120ms @1 RPS, ~210ms @5 RPS, ~420ms @10 RPS (these are from our dedicated pool baseline; we'll run the exact config for you).
- On limit hit: hosted API returns HTTP 429 by default; for Dedicated customers we can configure soft queuing (bounded queue) or immediate rejection depending on SLO preferences. We also support automated fallthrough to a cheaper, quantized variant if configured.
- Failover: Hosted customers get cross-region routing with automatic fallback to peer region (subject to capacity). Dedicated customers can opt into cross-region replication with active-active or warm-standby failover — the difference is RTO and cost.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood/Your team run a short interop experiment that compares error behavior at increasing RPS (1,5,10,25) vs your Vertex endpoint. We can run a 4-hour runbook and produce a failure-mode matrix.
2) We'll provide a short SLO summary.xlsx (attached) with recommended configs for soft-queueing vs reject behavior.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync with Logan (SRE) and Marissa (Reliability PM) to align test harness and metrics.

I attached the slides and a one-pager SLO summary; happy to iterate. When would be a good time for the sync?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — reliability/limits questions (test plan & SLO draft)

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. Short note and attached draft.

Planned interop test (high level):
- Duration: 4 hours active testing + 1 hour warmup/cooldown.
- Traffic profile: baseline steady-state at 5 RPS for 60m, ramp to target rates at 10m intervals, then run 6 x 10s bursts at 50 RPS spaced across the middle 90m. Payloads: 128-256 token prompts, mixture of short and medium outputs to simulate your production mix.
- Observability: we'll emit p50/p95/p99 latency, 429_count, 5xx_count, queue_length, kv_cache_hit_rate, failover_event. We'll push metrics to a shared Grafana and provide a Prometheus scrape endpoint you can ingest.
- Error budget: we compute a daily error budget where budget_consume = 429_count + 5xx_count (weighted) normalized to request volume; draft thresholds attached in redwood-slo-summary.xlsx. We'll also include a small JSON webhook you can subscribe to that indicates when reject-rate crosses 0.5% (configurable).
- Failover behavior doc: For Dedicated: warm-standby means <30s failover time, potential cold-cache penalty on first requests; active-active with cross-region replication keeps latency stable but doubles replication cost. We'll include annotated tradeoffs in the doc.

Next steps:
1) Confirm sync: Wed 09:30 PST — I can host and share the test harness repo in the drive link.
2) Ben will share ballpark POC pricing today so procurement has an initial figure.
3) Jordan: please confirm the burst schedule and whether you want us to coordinate load from Redwood only or both Redwood+Catalyst generators.

Happy to iterate on the SLO worksheet.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Reliability PM | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
